recipes.title: Chelow with Tahdig
recipes.description: Steamed Persian rice, every grain long and separate, over a golden crisp crust — the tahdig, which is what many people are actually there for.
instructions: Rinse the rice five times until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for at least two hours. This is what keeps the grains separate.
Boil a large pot of salted water, add the drained rice and cook 6–8 minutes only — soft outside, still firm at the core. Drain and rinse with lukewarm water.
Steep the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water. Slice the potato into half-centimetre rounds.
Heat the oil in the base of the pot and lay the potato slices in a single layer, dusted with turmeric — this is the tahdig.
Mound the rice on top in a pyramid, poke five holes through it with the handle of a wooden spoon, and drizzle over a little oil and the saffron water.
Wrap the lid in a tea towel, cover tightly and steam over very low heat for 50 minutes. Invert onto a large plate — tahdig on top.

recipes.title: Baghali Polo — Fava and Dill Rice
recipes.description: Green-and-white rice with fresh fava beans and an amount of dill that looks excessive until you taste it. The spring dish of Persia.
instructions: Soak the rice in salted water for two hours, then rinse and drain.
Blanch the favas for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water. If the outer skin is thick, slip it off.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes, drain and rinse.
Fold the drained rice together with the favas, dill and cinnamon — gently, so the grains stay whole.
Heat the oil in the pot, mound the mixture into a pyramid and poke holes through it. Pour over the saffron water.
Cover with a towel-wrapped lid and steam 45 minutes over very low heat.

recipes.title: Zereshk Polo — Barberry Rice
recipes.description: Saffron rice with sharp red barberries and flaked almonds. The colour alone explains why this is a dish for guests.
instructions: Soak the rice in salted water for two hours. Soak the barberries in cold water for 15 minutes — they carry grit — and drain well.
Boil the rice 6 minutes in salted water, drain and rinse.
Steam the rice in an oiled pot for 45 minutes under a towel-wrapped lid.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a small pan over low heat, add the barberries and sugar and fry for 60 seconds only — they burn instantly.
Lift out a cup of rice and stir it into the saffron water until it turns deep orange.
To serve: white rice as the base, the saffron rice over it, then scatter the barberries, almonds and pistachios.

recipes.title: Adas Polo — Lentil and Date Rice
recipes.description: Rice with brown lentils, raisins and caramelised dates. Sweet and savoury at once, and filling enough to stand alone.
instructions: Cook the lentils in water for 15 minutes — tender but whole — and drain.
Boil the soaked rice for 6 minutes in salted water, drain and rinse.
Fry the onions in oil until deeply golden, add the raisins and chopped dates and fry 3 minutes with the cinnamon.
Oil the pot and layer alternately: rice, lentils, the date mixture — finishing with rice.
Poke holes through, pour over the saffron water and a little oil.
Steam 45 minutes over very low heat under a towel-wrapped lid.

recipes.title: Sabzi Polo — Herb Rice
recipes.description: Rice turned deep green with parsley, coriander, dill and chives. Served at Nowruz, and at the Persian-Jewish seder.
instructions: Chop all the herbs very finely and dry them thoroughly — wet herbs turn the rice to porridge.
Boil the soaked rice 6 minutes in salted water, drain and rinse.
Fold the rice together with all the herbs and the fenugreek, gently.
Heat the oil in the pot and mound the mixture into a pyramid. Poke five holes through it.
Pour over the saffron water and a little oil, then cover with a towel-wrapped lid.
Steam 45 minutes over very low heat. Serve beside fish or meatballs.

recipes.title: Shirin Polo — Sweet Rice
recipes.description: Wedding rice: candied orange peel, carrot, almonds and pistachios. Sweet, golden, and meant for a large table.
instructions: Cut the orange peel into very thin strips and blanch three times in fresh boiling water — this removes the bitterness.
Make a syrup with 1/2 cup sugar and 1/2 cup water, add the peel and carrot and cook 10 minutes. Stir in the rosewater and cardamom.
Soak and boil the rice 6 minutes, drain and rinse.
Lightly toast the almonds and pistachios in a dry pan.
Layer rice and the citrus mixture in an oiled pot, finishing with rice. Poke holes and pour over the saffron water.
Steam 45 minutes over very low heat. Scatter the nuts before serving.

recipes.title: Lubia Polo — Green Bean and Meat Rice
recipes.description: Rice with green beans and ground lamb in a tomato and cinnamon sauce. A weekday dish that tastes like an occasion.
instructions: Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and the ground lamb and cook until browned.
Add the green beans, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, pepper and half a cup of water. Cook 20 minutes until the beans are tender and almost dry.
Soak and boil the rice 6 minutes in salted water, drain and rinse.
Oil the pot and layer rice and the meat mixture alternately, finishing with rice.
Poke holes through, pour over the saffron water and a little oil.
Steam 45 minutes over very low heat. No dairy at any stage.

recipes.title: Albaloo Polo — Sour Cherry Rice
recipes.description: Pink rice with sour cherries in syrup. The contrast between sweet and sharp is the whole point.
instructions: Cook the cherries with the sugar over low heat for 15 minutes. Strain and keep the syrup separately — it is for serving.
Reduce the syrup another 10 minutes until thick, then stir in the cardamom.
Soak and boil the rice 6 minutes, drain and rinse.
Oil the pot and layer rice and cherries, finishing with rice — the cherries stay inside so they do not scorch.
Poke holes, pour over the saffron water and steam 45 minutes over low heat.
Serve with the syrup poured over and flaked almonds scattered on top.

recipes.title: Kateh — Simple Rice
recipes.description: Rice the northern way: everything in one pot, no draining. Less ceremony than chelow, and it still gives you a tahdig.
instructions: Rinse the rice three times and drain. No long soak needed.
Put the rice, water, oil and salt in a pot and bring to the boil over medium heat.
Cook uncovered until the water is absorbed and the rice surfaces — about 10 minutes.
Turn the heat to its lowest, wrap the lid in a towel and cover.
Cook 30 minutes without opening. The base forms a thin, crisp tahdig.
Drizzle with the saffron water, fold gently and serve.

recipes.title: Dami Gojeh — Tomato Rice
recipes.description: Orange-red rice cooked together with fresh tomato and paste. A Monday-night rice that always gets finished.
instructions: Rinse the rice and soak it 30 minutes in salted water.
Fry the onion in oil until translucent, add the turmeric and paprika and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato paste and fry for a minute, then the grated tomatoes. Cook 10 minutes.
Add the drained rice, stir, and pour in the boiling water. Season.
Cook uncovered until the liquid is absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Reduce to the lowest heat, cover with a towel-wrapped lid and steam 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Ghormeh Sabzi
recipes.description: Iran's national dish: a sea of fried herbs, kidney beans, lamb and dried Persian lime. Dark green and sharply sour.
instructions: Fry the chopped herbs in a third of the oil over low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring. They must darken and shrink — this step decides the flavour of the whole dish and cannot be rushed.
In a separate pot fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and the meat and sear on all sides.
Add the soaked beans and water to cover. Bring to the boil and cook covered for an hour.
Add the fried herbs and the dried limes — pierce them with a fork first so they release their flavour.
Cook another hour and a half over low heat, until the meat falls apart and the sauce is dark and thick.
Season. If it is too sour, lift out one lime. Serve over chelow.

recipes.title: Fesenjan — Chicken in Walnut and Pomegranate
recipes.description: A deep brown-purple sauce of ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses. Sweet, sour and unusually rich.
instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 5 minutes until fragrant, cool and grind very finely in a processor.
Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and set aside. In the same pot sear the chicken legs until golden and remove.
Add the ground walnuts and the water to the pot and cook over very low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often — the walnut oil will rise to the surface, which is the sign it is ready.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses, sugar and cinnamon. The sauce will darken almost to chocolate brown.
Return the chicken and onion and cook covered another hour over low heat.
Season. Too sour, add sugar; too sweet, add molasses. Serve over white chelow.

recipes.title: Gheimeh — Yellow Split Pea Stew
recipes.description: A lamb stew with yellow split peas and dried lime, buried under a mountain of matchstick fried potatoes.
instructions: Soak the split peas in hot water for 30 minutes and drain.
Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and the meat and sear on all sides.
Add the tomato paste and fry a minute, then water to cover. Cook covered for an hour.
Add the split peas and the pierced limes and cook a further 40 minutes, until the peas are tender but not collapsing.
Cut the potatoes into thin matchsticks, dry them and deep-fry until golden and crisp.
Season, stir in the saffron water, and serve with the potatoes on top — added only at the table so they stay crisp.

recipes.title: Khoresht Bademjan — Eggplant Stew
recipes.description: Whole fried eggplants lying over a lamb and tomato stew, sharpened with verjuice or lemon.
instructions: Peel the eggplants in stripes, halve them lengthwise, salt and leave 30 minutes. Pat thoroughly dry — this is what stops them drinking oil.
Fry the eggplants until golden and soft on both sides. Drain on paper.
Fry the onion until golden, add the turmeric and the meat and sear.
Add the tomato paste, grated tomatoes and water to cover. Cook covered 75 minutes.
Lay the fried eggplants over the meat — do not stir, so they stay whole — and add the verjuice.
Cook another 20 minutes over low heat. Stir in the saffron water and serve over chelow.

recipes.title: Khoresht Karafs — Celery Stew
recipes.description: Celery, mint and parsley in a sour lamb stew. Green, fragrant, and unlike any other celery dish.
instructions: Fry the mint and parsley in oil over low heat for 10 minutes until darkened and fragrant.
In a separate pot fry the onion until golden, add the turmeric and the meat and sear all over.
Add water to cover and cook covered for an hour.
Fry the celery in oil for 8 minutes until it colours lightly at the edges — do not cook it soft.
Add the celery, the fried herbs, the pierced limes and the lemon juice to the pot.
Cook a further 40 minutes. The celery should keep some bite. Serve over chelow.

recipes.title: Khoresht Rivas — Rhubarb Stew
recipes.description: Sharp rhubarb in a lamb stew with mint and parsley. A late-spring dish most of the world has never met.
instructions: Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and the meat and sear.
Add water to cover and cook covered 70 minutes until the meat is tender.
Fry the mint and parsley in oil for 8 minutes and add to the pot.
Cut the rhubarb into 4cm lengths. Fry it briefly, 2 minutes only — it collapses very fast.
Add the rhubarb and sugar to the pot and cook 15–20 minutes without stirring much.
Season and stir in the saffron water. The rhubarb should still be in recognisable pieces.

recipes.title: Khoresht Aloo — Prune Stew
recipes.description: Lamb with dried prunes and saffron. Sweet, gentle, and the dish you serve to someone who does not like heat.
instructions: Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and the cinnamon stick.
Add the meat cubes and sear on all sides.
Add water to cover, bring to the boil and cook covered for 90 minutes.
Soak the prunes in hot water for 20 minutes and drain.
Add the prunes, sugar and saffron water and cook 25 minutes over low heat.
Finish with the lemon juice and season. The sauce should be thick and glossy.

recipes.title: Abgoosht — Dizi
recipes.description: A lamb and chickpea pot served as two courses from one vessel: the broth first, then the solids mashed to a paste.
instructions: Put the lamb, chickpeas, beans, onions and turmeric in a heavy pot and cover with water. Bring to the boil and skim.
Cook covered over low heat for two and a half hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Add the whole potatoes, tomato paste and pierced limes. Cook a further 40 minutes.
Strain the liquid into a bowl — this is the "ab", the broth, served first with bread.
Remove the bones and mash the meat, pulses and potatoes to a coarse paste — this is the "goosht".
Serve the paste as the second course, with raw onion, pickles and flatbread.

recipes.title: Khoresht Beh — Quince Stew
recipes.description: Caramelised quince in a lamb stew with split peas. The smell of the quince fills the whole house.
instructions: Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and the meat and sear on all sides.
Add water to cover and cook covered 70 minutes. Add the split peas and cook a further 25 minutes.
Halve the quinces, core them and cut into thick wedges. Hold in lemon water so they do not darken.
Fry the quince wedges in oil with the sugar until golden and caramelised on both sides.
Lay the quince over the meat, add the cinnamon and lemon juice, and cook together 25 minutes.
Stir in the saffron water and season. The quince should be tender but still holding.

recipes.title: Khoresht Loobia Sabz — Green Bean Stew
recipes.description: Green beans and beef in a tomato and turmeric sauce. The simplest stew on this list, and one of the most common at home.
instructions: Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the turmeric and the beef and sear.
Add the tomato paste and fry a minute, then the grated tomatoes and water to cover.
Cook covered for 60 minutes until the beef softens.
Fry the green beans separately in oil for 5 minutes — this keeps their colour.
Add the beans to the pot with the cinnamon and cook a further 25 minutes.
Season. The sauce should be thick, not watery.

recipes.title: Kabab Koobideh
recipes.description: Ground meat with grated onion, pressed onto a flat skewer and grilled over coals. The kabab every other one is measured against.
instructions: Grate the onion finely and squeeze it dry in a cloth — wet onion makes the meat fall off the skewer. This is the critical step.
Knead both meats with the squeezed onion, sumac, turmeric, salt and pepper for 10 minutes, until the mixture turns sticky and uniform.
Chill at least an hour — cold meat grips better.
Wet your hands in salted water, take a ball of meat and press it along a wide flat skewer, ridging it with your fingers.
Grill over hot coals 4 minutes a side, turning constantly. Do not walk away from the skewer.
Grill tomatoes and peppers alongside. Serve over chelow with saffron water and sumac.

recipes.title: Kabab Barg
recipes.description: Thin fillet slices in an onion, lemon and saffron marinade. The name means "leaf", after the shape.
instructions: Slice the meat into thin 1cm slices and flatten them lightly with a mallet.
Make the marinade: grated and squeezed onion, lemon juice, olive oil, pepper and half the saffron water. **No salt** — salt at this stage dries the meat out.
Marinate at least 4 hours in the fridge, overnight if possible.
Thread each slice lengthwise onto a flat skewer, like a ribbon.
Grill over strong coals 4–5 minutes a side only. The meat is thin and burns fast.
Salt only at the end, brush with the remaining saffron water and serve with sumac.

recipes.title: Joojeh Kabab — Saffron Chicken Kabab
recipes.description: Golden-yellow chicken from a saffron, lemon and onion marinade. The common marinade is yogurt-based; this one is lemon-based, which keeps the dish meat.
instructions: Steep the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water for 15 minutes.
Make the marinade: squeezed grated onion, lemon juice, olive oil, pepper and half the saffron water. **No yogurt** — this version is traditional, and it keeps the dish meat.
Add the chicken cubes to the marinade and chill at least 4 hours.
Thread onto skewers alternating with cherry tomatoes.
Grill over medium coals 8–10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes.
Brush with the remaining saffron water in the last minutes, salt, and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Kabab Chenjeh
recipes.description: Lamb cubes with almost no spice — onion, lemon and pepper. The meat has to be good enough to stand on its own.
instructions: Cut the lamb into 3cm cubes, leaving a little fat on each.
Mix with the grated onion, lemon juice, oil and pepper. No salt.
Marinate 4 hours in the fridge.
Thread tightly onto skewers with no vegetables between — meat should touch meat.
Grill over strong coals 5–7 minutes, turning every ninety seconds.
Salt at the end and serve with sliced fresh onion and sumac.

recipes.title: Shishlik — Lamb Chops
recipes.description: Whole lamb chops on the bone, grilled until the fat crisps. The signature dish of Shandiz.
instructions: Trim the chops but leave the fat — it is what makes them crisp.
Mix the squeezed grated onion, lemon juice, olive oil, pepper and saffron water.
Marinate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, turning once.
Lay the chops directly on the charcoal grill, not on a skewer.
Grill 8–9 minutes a side over medium heat — rendering fat will flare, so keep moving them and do not walk away.
Salt with coarse salt at the end and serve with lemon wedges and chelow.

recipes.title: Kabab Torsh — Sour Kabab from Gilan
recipes.description: A northern kabab in a walnut and pomegranate marinade. Sour, nutty and dark — unlike any other kabab.
instructions: Blitz the walnuts, garlic, coriander and pomegranate molasses to a thick paste.
Stir in the olive oil and pepper. The marinade should be dark and viscous.
Rub the meat cubes in the paste and refrigerate **at least 12 hours** — the pomegranate acid is what tenderises the meat.
Shake off the excess marinade and thread onto skewers.
Grill over medium coals 6–8 minutes, turning every two minutes. The marinade scorches fast over high heat.
Salt at the end and serve with chelow and red onion.

recipes.title: Kabab Bakhtiari
recipes.description: One skewer alternating lamb and chicken. Two textures, two marinades, a single skewer.
instructions: Divide the grated onion between two bowls. To the lamb add pepper and oil; to the chicken add turmeric and saffron water.
Add lemon juice to both and marinate separately for 4 hours — chicken and lamb cook differently, so the marinades differ too.
Thread alternately onto one skewer: lamb, chicken, lamb, chicken.
Grill over medium coals, starting with the lamb end nearer the hot centre.
Grill 8–9 minutes a side, turning often.
Brush with saffron, salt and serve over chelow.

recipes.title: Mahi Kabab — Grilled Fish
recipes.description: White fish in a saffron, garlic and coriander marinade, grilled over coals. Fin-and-scale fish only — the dish is parve.
instructions: Cut the fillets into 5cm pieces, keeping the skin on.
Mix the garlic, coriander, lime juice, olive oil, turmeric, saffron water and pepper.
Marinate the fish 45 minutes only — longer and the acid starts to "cook" it.
Thread onto flat skewers, or lay on an oiled grill rack.
Grill over medium coals 5–6 minutes a side only. Turn once.
Salt at the end and serve with sabzi polo and lime. Fin-and-scale fish only.

recipes.title: Kabab Tabei — Pan Kabab
recipes.description: The koobideh mixture, made in a pan with no skewers. What you make when there are no coals and there is hunger.
instructions: Knead the meat with the squeezed onion, turmeric, sumac, salt and pepper for 8 minutes until sticky.
Press the whole mixture into an even layer in a large oiled pan.
Score it into squares with a knife — it will then break cleanly when served.
Fry covered over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the base is golden.
Turn it carefully using a plate, lay tomato slices on top and fry a further 10 minutes.
Drizzle with saffron water and serve straight from the pan with bread or rice.

recipes.title: Shami Kabab — Meat and Split Pea Patties
recipes.description: Flat patties of meat and ground yellow split peas, with a hole in the middle. Travel food — they are good cold too.
instructions: Cook the split peas in water for 40 minutes until very soft. Drain thoroughly and dry.
Blitz the peas with the ground beef and onion to a smooth, sticky paste.
Add the eggs, turmeric, cinnamon, cumin, salt and pepper and mix. Chill 30 minutes.
Form balls with damp hands, flatten into 1cm rounds and press a hole through the centre with a finger.
Shallow-fry 4–5 minutes a side until browned.
Drain on paper. Serve hot or cold with bread, pickles and lemon.

recipes.title: Gondi — Chicken and Chickpea Dumplings
recipes.description: Dumplings of chickpea flour and ground chicken, poached in clear broth. The Shabbat dish of Iranian Jews, and it has no equivalent.
instructions: Grate the onion finely and squeeze it dry. Wet onion will break the dumplings apart as they cook.
Knead the ground chicken, chickpea flour, squeezed onion, cardamom, turmeric, oil, salt and pepper for 10 minutes to a smooth, sticky paste.
Chill at least 30 minutes — this is what holds the balls together.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer with the whole onion and the pierced limes.
Form walnut-sized balls with wet hands and lower them carefully into the simmering broth.
Cook covered over low heat for 60 minutes without stirring. They rise to the surface when done. Serve in a bowl with the broth, flatbread and fresh herbs.

recipes.title: Ash-e Anar — Pomegranate Soup
recipes.description: A thick soup of herbs, rice and lentils in a sour pomegranate broth. Pink-brown, and it serves autumn in a bowl.
instructions: Fry the onions in oil until deeply golden, add the turmeric and set half aside for the garnish.
Add the rice, lentils and split peas to the pot with 1.5 litres of water. Cook 40 minutes.
Add all the chopped herbs and cook a further 20 minutes — the soup will darken.
Add the pomegranate juice, molasses and sugar. Cook 25 minutes uncovered over low heat.
Taste and balance: more molasses for sharpness, more sugar for sweetness. It should be thick.
Serve with the fried onion and fresh pomegranate seeds on top.

recipes.title: Ash-e Jo — Parve Barley Soup
recipes.description: A barley and pulse soup with herbs. The traditional version is served with kashk; this one is parve, with nothing put in its place.
instructions: Fry the onions in oil until golden. Set a third aside for the garnish and stir the dried mint into it.
Add the turmeric to the pot, then the barley, lentils and beans and 2 litres of water.
Cook covered 60 minutes until the barley is tender and the soup begins to thicken.
Add all the herbs and cook a further 25 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. If too thick, add boiling water.
Serve with the fried onion and mint on top. Fully parve — it works beside a dairy course too.

recipes.title: Soup-e Jo — Barley and Chicken Soup
recipes.description: A smooth barley soup with carrot, chicken and lemon. The restaurant version is thickened with cream; this one uses broth alone, so it stays meat.
instructions: Cook the chicken legs in 2 litres of water with half the onion for 40 minutes. Strain the broth and pull the meat from the bone.
Fry the remaining onion in oil until translucent, add the turmeric.
Add the strained broth, the barley, carrot and potato. Cook 30 minutes.
Blend about a third of the soup and return it — this gives a velvety texture with no cream.
Return the shredded chicken and warm through for 5 minutes.
Season with salt, white pepper and lemon juice, and stir in the parsley. No dairy here.

recipes.title: Kuku Sabzi — Herb Frittata
recipes.description: More herb than egg, so dark green it is nearly black, with barberries and walnuts. It sits on the Persian-Jewish seder table.
instructions: Chop all the herbs finely and dry them well between towels — wet herbs make a slimy kuku.
Beat the eggs and add the flour, baking powder, turmeric, salt and pepper.
Fold in all the herbs, the barberries and the walnuts. It should look like herbs held together by egg, not the other way round.
Heat the oil in a medium pan and pour in the whole mixture, spreading it evenly.
Cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes, until the base is golden and the centre almost set.
Turn it with a plate and cook a further 10 minutes. Serve hot or at room temperature, cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Kuku Sibzamini — Potato Kuku
recipes.description: Grated potato and egg with saffron and turmeric. Plain, golden, and eaten hot or straight from the fridge.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 25 minutes until tender. Cool, peel and grate coarsely.
Squeeze the grated onion dry.
Beat the eggs with the flour, baking powder, turmeric, saffron water, salt and pepper.
Fold in the potato and onion — gently, so they do not turn to mash.
Cook in an oiled pan, covered, for 12 minutes over low heat.
Turn with a plate and cook a further 10 minutes until golden. Cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Kuku Bademjan — Eggplant Kuku
recipes.description: Roasted, mashed eggplant bound with egg, turmeric and garlic. Deep and smoky, nothing like the green kuku.
instructions: Roast the eggplants at 220°C for about 35 minutes until fully collapsed. Cool, peel and mash.
Drain the mashed flesh in a sieve for 15 minutes — the bitter liquid has to go.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until golden, add the turmeric and dried mint.
Beat the eggs with the flour, baking powder, salt and pepper, and fold in the eggplant and onion.
Pour into an oiled pan and cook covered 15 minutes over low heat.
Turn and cook a further 10 minutes. Serve with flatbread and herbs.

recipes.title: Eshkeneh — Onion and Egg Soup
recipes.description: A rustic soup of fried onion, fenugreek and egg whisked in at the end. Five ingredients, and unreasonably comforting.
instructions: Fry the onion in oil over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, until brown and sweet. That is the entire base.
Add the turmeric and flour and stir for a minute — the flour will thicken the soup.
Add the fenugreek and pour in the boiling water gradually, stirring, to avoid lumps.
Cook 12 minutes over low heat and season with salt and pepper.
Beat the eggs in a bowl, lower the heat and pour them in slowly while stirring constantly — they should shred into threads, not set into curds.
Finish with lemon juice and serve at once with bread.

recipes.title: Ash-e Sholeh Ghalamkar — Everything Soup
recipes.description: A thick soup with four pulses, rice and four herbs. The name refers to printed cloth — because everything goes in.
instructions: Fry the onions in oil for 20 minutes until deeply brown. Set half aside and stir the dried mint into it.
Add the turmeric to the pot, then all the soaked pulses and 2.5 litres of water. Cook an hour.
Add the rice and cook a further 20 minutes.
Add all the herbs and the spinach and cook 30 minutes — it should thicken until a spoon nearly stands in it.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Serve with the fried onion and mint on top. A soup for a crowd.

recipes.title: Ab-Doogh Khiar — Cold Yogurt Soup
recipes.description: A cold summer soup of yogurt, cucumber, raisins and walnuts. The one dairy recipe in this category.
instructions: Soak the raisins in hot water for 10 minutes and drain.
Whisk the yogurt with the cold water in a large bowl until smooth and pourable.
Add the cucumber, raisins, walnuts, dill, spring onion and dried mint.
Season and chill at least two hours — it has to be very cold.
Tear the dry bread into coarse crumbs and stir them in just before serving, so they do not dissolve.
Serve with ice cubes. **A dairy recipe** — not for a meat meal.

recipes.title: Shirazi Salad
recipes.description: Cucumber, tomato and onion in tiny dice with lime and dried mint. The salad that reaches every Persian table.
instructions: Cut the cucumber, tomato and onion into tiny, evenly sized dice — that is the whole secret, and the knife matters more than the ingredients.
Scoop out the tomato seeds if they are very watery, so the salad does not go soupy.
Toss in a bowl with the lime juice, olive oil, dried mint and sumac.
Season with salt and pepper only just before serving, since salt draws out liquid.
Chill 20 minutes.
Toss again and serve cold, with a slotted spoon so the liquid stays in the bowl.

recipes.title: Mast-o Khiar — Yogurt and Cucumber
recipes.description: Thick yogurt with cucumber, raisins, walnuts and dried rose petals. A dairy recipe.
instructions: Strain the yogurt in a cloth for 30 minutes if it is loose — it needs to be very thick.
Soak the raisins in hot water 10 minutes, drain and dry.
Dice the cucumbers small. If watery, salt them lightly and drain for 10 minutes.
Fold the yogurt together with the cucumber, raisins, half the walnuts, dill and dried mint.
Season with salt and chill an hour.
Serve with the remaining walnuts, rose petals and olive oil on top. **Dairy** — not beside a meat course.

recipes.title: Borani Esfenaj — Spinach in Yogurt
recipes.description: Cooked spinach with garlic folded into thick yogurt. Green and white, and always asked for again. A dairy recipe.
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for a minute, drain and refresh in cold water.
Squeeze the spinach hard — this matters, or the dish turns watery — and chop roughly.
Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft, add the spinach and cook 5 minutes. Cool completely.
Fold the cold spinach into the yogurt — if the spinach is warm the yogurt will split.
Season with salt, pepper and dried mint. Chill an hour.
Serve with walnuts and olive oil on top. **Dairy.**

recipes.title: Torshi Liteh — Minced Pickles
recipes.description: Eggplant, vegetables and herbs minced into vinegar and cured for two months. Sour, hot and addictive.
instructions: Roast the eggplants until fully soft, peel and drain in a sieve for an hour — any liquid left will spoil the cure.
Chop the carrot, cauliflower, peppers and garlic very finely, or pulse briefly in a processor.
Mix everything with the eggplant flesh, mint, fenugreek, coriander seed and salt.
Add the vinegar gradually to a thick but pourable paste.
Pack into sterilised jars, making sure a centimetre of vinegar covers everything — this is what prevents mould.
Seal and leave somewhere cool and dark for **two months** before opening.

recipes.title: Mirza Ghasemi — Smoked Eggplant
recipes.description: Eggplant charred over flame with garlic, tomato and egg. The signature dish of Gilan, and genuinely smoky.
instructions: Char the eggplants directly over an open flame until the skin is completely black and the flesh soft — the smoke is the dish, and an oven will not give you it.
Peel and mash the flesh with a fork, not a processor. The texture should stay coarse.
Fry the garlic in oil for 30 seconds only, until fragrant.
Add the mashed eggplant and turmeric and fry 8 minutes, stirring.
Add the grated tomato and paste and cook 12 minutes until the liquid reduces.
Crack in the eggs and stir for 2 minutes until they set through the mixture. **Parve** — there is no butter here.

recipes.title: Halek — Persian Charoset
recipes.description: Dates, walnuts, almonds and pistachios in a thick paste with cinnamon and pomegranate. The charoset of Iranian Jews.
instructions: Toast the walnuts, almonds and pistachios in a dry pan for 5 minutes until fragrant. Cool.
Grind the nuts coarsely in a processor — keep a few halves back for decoration.
If the dates are dry, soak them in hot water for 10 minutes and pat dry.
Blitz the dates to a sticky paste, then add the ground nuts.
Fold in the pomegranate molasses, cinnamon, cardamom and rosewater. The mixture should be thick and dark.
Press into a serving bowl and decorate with whole walnuts. Keeps two weeks refrigerated.

recipes.title: Sholeh Zard — Saffron Rice Pudding
recipes.description: A rice pudding glowing yellow with saffron, scented with rosewater and cardamom. Not a drop of milk — entirely parve.
instructions: Rinse the rice and soak two hours. Drain.
Cook the rice in 6 cups of water over low heat for 50 minutes, until the grains break down completely.
Steep the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water.
Add the sugar and cook 20 minutes, stirring — only once the rice is soft, because sugar added early stops it softening.
Add the oil, saffron water, rosewater and cardamom. Cook a further 15 minutes until thick and glossy.
Pour into bowls, cool, and decorate with cinnamon, almonds and pistachios. **Parve** — it can follow a meat meal.

recipes.title: Faloodeh Shirazi
recipes.description: A frozen dessert of fine rice noodles in lime and rosewater syrup. Ice without dairy, and centuries old.

ingredients.name: sour cherries in syrup, to serve

instructions: Make the syrup: bring the water and sugar to the boil, then simmer 10 minutes. Cool completely and stir in the rosewater.
Boil the rice noodles 2–3 minutes only, drain and rinse in cold water.
Cut the noodles into 3cm lengths.
Stir the noodles into the cold syrup and transfer to a shallow tray.
Freeze 3–4 hours, raking with a fork every 45 minutes to build a grainy, granita-like texture.
Serve in glasses with fresh lime juice squeezed over and sour cherries. **Parve.**

recipes.title: Bastani Sonnati — Saffron Ice Cream
recipes.description: Persian ice cream with saffron, rosewater and pistachios, shot through with frozen cream flakes. A dairy recipe.
instructions: Steep the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot milk for 20 minutes.
Heat the milk and cream to just below boiling. Whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale.
Pour the hot milk into the yolks in a thin stream, whisking constantly — temper it, or the yolks will scramble.
Return to low heat and stir until the custard coats a spoon, about 8 minutes. **Do not boil.**
Add the saffron milk, rosewater and cardamom. Cool completely and chill 4 hours.
Churn in an ice cream maker. Separately freeze the extra cream in a thin layer, break into flakes and fold in with the pistachios. **Dairy.**

recipes.title: Ranginak — Date and Walnut Squares
recipes.description: Dates stuffed with walnuts under a blanket of flour toasted in oil with cinnamon. A southern sweet with no baking.
instructions: Open each date lengthwise and press a walnut half inside. Close it gently.
Pack the stuffed dates in a single tight layer in a square tin.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the flour gradually.
Toast the flour over medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring constantly, until light brown and smelling nutty. This is the step that decides it — under-toasted flour leaves a raw taste.
Take off the heat, stir in the cinnamon and cardamom, and pour the hot flour over the dates. Level it with a spoon.
Cool completely, dust with icing sugar and pistachios and cut into squares. **Parve.**
